title: Making an Alexander the Great (and/or Rome?) Total War meets Mount & Blade style game. Any ideas?
author: Odd-Score2887
selftext:
Hey guys, 

**I want to make an Alexander the Great** (and/or Rome?) **Total War meets Imperator and Mount & Blade style game.** 

Basic features, map and war will work like Total War and Imperator: Rome. Actual combat will be a mix between Total War and Mount & Blade. 

If you have played these games, what are you missing from them? Something you would find cool and fun? 

I have some ideas myself including much more in depth stories, quests, more city building, more advanced economies and some Mount & Blade style governing of cities (maybe walkable), slowly building up an army (not just bying units) and POV combat. 

I dont want it to just be the total war campagin where you buy units and attack over and over again.

Basically, I want to take the best of all these games and bring it together but in the age of Alexander the Great and/or Rome. Not sure yet, which time period would be the most fun. On one hand, Alexander the Great feels like an unexplored "world", but a game set in Rome would be interesting as well as you could have the whole republic/senate/politics part included as well in a more in depth angle.  

Look forward to hearing some ideas if you have any!

comments.author: Safe-Industry2465
comments.body:
I believe most of these games have a few mistakes that prevent them from becoming great.
Funnily enough, the combination you picked should cover the weaknesses of each other.

However, balancing is a nightmare. Believable world is a nightmare. Grind that respects your time and not being repetitive is a nightmare.
